summary: A deeply divided Fed held rates steady last week, splitting 8-4 — the most dissent since 1992 — as policymakers clashed over whether rate cuts remain appropriate amid sticky inflation. Adding to policy uncertainty, Powell's nominated successor Kevin Warsh is set to take the chair on May 15, keeping bond markets on edge and suppressing duration appetite.
tweet: Fed's historic 8-4 split and an imminent Powell-to-Warsh handover are rattling bonds, while pre-summit U.S.-China trade hopes keep stocks in greed territory despite thin breadth.
